bug_semantics: CWE-770 HTTP/2 connection-window starvation: when a stream's response body outruns the connection send window (default 65,535 bytes, shared across streams), Bandit.HTTP2.Connection queues the remaining bytes plus a reply closure in pending_sends and the stream/Plug process blocks forever inside GenServer.call(..., :infinity) to the connection process. The queue drains only on connection-level WINDOW_UPDATE/SETTINGS; nothing bounds the wait and nothing purges the queue. A client RST_STREAM is delivered to the blocked stream's mailbox but is never read while stuck in the call, so cancel frees nothing; periodic PINGs keep the transport read timeout from firing. Each stalled stream pins its process, Plug state, and any resource held across the write (e.g. a pooled upstream connection). Stream-window waits were later bounded at 15s; the connection-window path was not. Affects bandit 0.3.4 through 1.12.4.
flaw_origin: First written in 6feadb31189d18b7dcda6c663112cd3bbaf63a46 (Implement send flow control, 2021-09-13). That commit added Connection.pending_sends, Handler :noreply + on_unblock when either send window is exhausted, and changed Adapter.send_data from default-timeout GenServer.call/3 to GenServer.call(..., :infinity). Immediate parent 7a53ff9c37aafb05e4c37de0a6c9f5fbc919f117 sent DATA immediately with a 5s default call timeout and had no pending_sends, so a blocked send could not pin a stream indefinitely. Later H2 refactors (ba755c03 / reintroduced fff06efe) moved the :infinity call into Stream.send_data/3 and bounded stream-window waits; finish_data/5 (b2b43570) only extracted the existing enqueue. Those are moves/refactors of the same mechanism, not a new BIC.
